text:
Alex Kim: Heads-up — we need to backfill cert automation for several older services in eu-west and ap-southeast. Current cert-manager SA doesn't have the KMS wrapping permissions. Also our recent vuln scan flagged legacy cipher support on a couple frontends. Can we coordinate RBAC + KMS + audit logging changes before we do a wide rollout?

Priya Rao: @Alex Kim thanks. do you have a list of services? I can start a permissions matrix. prefer to keep per-region KMS keys if it simplifies compliance. :+1:

Alex Kim: quick list: search-api-eu, telemetry-proxy-ap, billing-worker (shared region config). I sketched an approach: 1) create per-region KMS key rings, 2) grant cert-manager SA Encrypt/Decrypt on keys, 3) add audit log sink for key operations to our secure GCS bucket, 4) RBAC PR to limit SA tokens to namespace. Thoughts?

Samir Patel: sounds good. a couple notes:
- per-region keys reduce blast radius and match regs. replicate secrets only where needed.
- Cert automation: use keyVersion for explicit rotations, but need a migration strategy for existing certs wrapped with old key.
- For audit: include key id and principal in logs, push to SIEM with retention 7 years for eu.

Priya Rao: migration idea — backfill: issue new certs wrapped with new key and perform rolling swap with canary podset. do not revoke old key until audit confirms no callers rely on it. Ops should also run a dry-run ACL check.

eng-security-bot: vuln-scan results uploaded: openssl-legacy-ciphers detected on telemetry-proxy-ap (CVSS 6.1). See: https://internal/reports/scan/1803456789

Alex Kim: Ugh. that explains the scan noise. we should harden TLS config before cert swap. proposed nginx tls block: 
```
ssl_protocols TLSv1.2 TLSv1.3;
ssl_prefer_server_ciphers off;
ssl_ciphers 'TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256:TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384:TLS_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256';
ssl_session_tickets off;
ssl_session_cache shared:SSL:10m;
add_header Strict-Transport-Security "max-age=63072000; includeSubDomains; preload" always;
```
Will that break any old internal clients?

Samir Patel: should be fine for public-facing. run a compatibility test for internal batch clients — some older JVMs won't support TLS1.3 cipher suites. fallback rule: place an edge-proxy with agreed ciphers and allow TLS1.2 for legacy clients in restricted subnets only.

Priya Rao: RBAC bits — I drafted a PR to add KMS permissions and tightened namespace role for cert-manager: https://git.internal/r/redwood/infra/+/branches/cert-kms-backfill . It includes a dry-run script to simulate permission checks. Can infra-owners review?

Alex Kim: linking the PR in the deploy ticket and tagging infra-owners. ops, can you add an auditbot watcher so we get a message when a key is used in production during rollout?

ops-deploy-bot: Added watcher: kms-key-usage to #eng-security and will post aggregated events every 10m. Alert thresholds: >10 uses/min => pager.

Samir Patel: for vuln triage on the openssl finding: we should open a short-lifecycle incident with severity S2, assign to telemetry team, mitigate by upgrading the base image in the canary, and then run re-scan. keep cert swap blocked until re-scan passes.

Alex Kim: Agreed. I'll open the incident and set the runbook steps: 1) apply nginx config on canary, 2) upgrade base image to openssl-1.1.1+ or BoringSSL build, 3) validate metrics and connection counts, 4) roll out regionally.

Priya Rao: small RBAC caveat — cert-manager SA tokens are currently clusterRoleBound in a few clusters for legacy reasons. we must remove cluster-wide bindings and create namespace-level roles before giving KMS access. otherwise we'll grant KMS to more workloads than intended.

Alex Kim: good catch. add that to the PR checklist and the incident runbook.

eng-security-bot: audit-sink created: gs://secure-audit-bucket/kms/2024-05/ (policy: encrypted, restricted access).

Samir Patel: one last ops note — add a metric for key-wrap latency to our SLO dashboard. if KMS latency spikes during heavy cert churn, we should fallback to a short-lived cert cache to avoid token bloat and throttling.

Alex Kim: thanks all — action items: Priya to review permissions matrix, Samir to own canary TLS test, ops to vet PR and enable audit watcher, I'll run the incident for the vuln triage and coordinate rollout. Will post updates here. :rocket:
